verdicts.reasoning: Both texts record the same court notice. Each reads 'NOTICE FROM THE COURT: INSTRUCTIONS FOR CIVIL CASES ASSIGNED TO THE HONORABLE ELEANOR L. ROSS.' and was docketed by the same clerk (mlb) with the same filing date, 01/28/2026. It is the same kind of entry (a court notice) about the same document (Judge Ross's civil-case instructions) from the same filer on the same day. The twin's text (451857584, unnumbered) appears word for word at the start of entry #12's text (452037636). #12 adds only a second '(mlb)' and the stamp '(Entered: 01/28/2026)', so the short form names nothing that #12 does not. A clerk would read the repeated initials to mean the same clerk carried #12's text over from the unnumbered entry, either by editing it or by docketing it again with the document attached. The record supports that: CourtListener captured the unnumbered notice at 09:56 PT on 01/28, between #5 and #6 in creation order, but #12's number comes after #11, so the numbered version came from a later action that same day. That fits the unnumbered object being an earlier capture of this same notice. The record cannot show whether the court's docket still keeps the unnumbered line as a separate duplicate, but nothing in either text points to a different event. No other object in the 01/27 to 01/29 window fits the twin as well. The other unnumbered objects dated 01/28 are clerk's notations about entries 4 and 7 and an 'Order' whose text comes from a document, and none of them is a notice of instructions.

I checked all 20 objects in the 01/27 to 01/29 window. The twin (451857584) reads 'NOTICE FROM THE COURT: INSTRUCTIONS FOR CIVIL CASES ASSIGNED TO THE HONORABLE ELEANOR L. ROSS. (mlb)'. That is a word-for-word prefix of the long form, #12 (452037636), which only adds '(mlb). (Entered: 01/28/2026)'. The only other notice in the window is #5 (451857582), a Notice of Appearance filed by attorney Bryan Tyson for Raffensperger. That is a party filing, not a notice from the court, so it does not fit. The other numbered entries (#2-#4, #6-#11) are a summons, motions to intervene, disclosure certificates and pro hac vice applications. The unnumbered objects are clerk's notations re 4 and re 7, clerk's-office pro hac vice approvals, a bare 'Order' document (451865808) and a pro hac vice approval document (452134020). None of them could be the judge's case-assignment instructions. #12 is the only numbered entry in the window the twin can describe. One timing oddity: the twin was created 01/28 09:56 in the same batch as #3-#7, between #5 and #6, while #12 was created 01/29 and is numbered after the pro hac vice applications #8-#11. Together with the doubled '(mlb) (mlb)' in #12, this fits the same entry being edited or renumbered later. It does not point to any other entry in the window.

The clocks point to two separate docketing acts rather than one entry seen twice, but the record does not show whether the first act still stands on the docket. (1) The twin 451857584 has no entry number, desc_source 'entry', time_filed null and date_created 2026-01-28T09:56:04.454-08:00. The entry 452037636 is #12, desc_source 'entry', time_filed null, date_created 2026-01-29T11:36:36.910-08:00. That is about 25h40m apart, not minutes. Both have entry_at 2026-01-28 and neither is twin_of any other object. (2) The twin was created in the 09:56:03.979 to 09:56:04.607 batch that also created #3 to #7. Its id falls between #5 (451857582, 09:56:04.248) and #6 (451857585, 09:56:04.504), right after the unnumbered Clerk's Notation re 4 (451857583). So the notice was on the docket without a number, between #5 and #6, at that time. (3) #8 to #11 were first created later, at 2026-01-28T11:29:34 to 11:35:06, about 1h33m after the twin. Docket numbers are assigned in order, so number 12 was given after #11. That is a later docketing act than the one the twin captured, so the twin cannot be a capture of #12. (4) The shape is also unusual: both objects are docket-entry objects, not a RECAP document object paired with its docket text. (5) The same notice text appears twice: first without a number and with document_url null, then as #12, whose text doubles the clerk's initials ('(mlb) (mlb). (Entered: 01/28/2026)'). The doubled initials suggest the same clerk re-docketed or edited the notice. The record cannot tell whether the earlier unnumbered entry was turned into #12 or removed (one entry seen in two states), or still stands beside #12 (two entries). The clocks do not support a link. (6) No other object in the window has this text. The unnumbered 'Order' document 451865808 (created 2026-01-28T10:34:05) does not fit it, so there is no better match.

The case designation is: 1:25-cv-371-AJ ... (ed)'. The short form is fully consistent with it and names nothing the long form does not do (no other judge, party, motion or document). Both objects are dated 2025-09-25 and both are unnumbered, so their fingerprints agree. 439194969 is the only case-assignment long text in the 09/24-09/26 window. The other candidates fit worse. Entry 4 (439090829, 'NOTICE of Assignment to U.S. Magistrate Judge and Consent Form sent to plaintiff...') is a separate, numbered notice and consent-form entry, a different event, and a short form of it would carry no. 4. Entry 3 (438945550, text null) is numbered and was filed at 11:59:33 among counsel's opening filings, while the twin is unnumbered. The other 'Case Assigned' object, 439090834 (dated 09/26, 13:03:14, created that day next to 'Notice - ECF' 439090820 at 13:06:10), is itself a short form. No case-assignment long text dated 09/26 exists for it. It most plausibly records this same assignment under its entry time: entry 4 likewise carries a 09/25 date but reads 'Entered: 09/26/2025'. That makes it a second short form of the same minute entry, not a distinct event the twin belongs to. Its 09/26 date also fits the twin's 09/25 date worse than the long form does. Even if 439090834 were a distinct 09/26 event, the twin's 09/25 date would still point to 439194969. No better match.
